points: Job says his breath is corrupt, his days are extinct, and the graves are ready for him.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: He is surrounded by mockers, and his eye continues in their provocation, so his complaint is that even now the men around him do not comfort him but scorn him.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: Job has been made a byword of the people, a man in whose face others spit, and by reason of sorrow all his members are as a shadow.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: Even so, upright men shall be astonished at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: The righteous shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger, so the trial does not turn the righteous back but presses him forward.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: Job's purposes are broken off and the thoughts of his heart are undone, so that he speaks as a man with no future left in this life.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: He has made his bed in the darkness, called corruption his father and the worm his mother and sister, and asks where his hope now is.

note.label: Job 17: My Days Are Extinct, the Graves Are Ready for Me

points: His hope goes down with him to the bars of the pit, when their rest together is in the dust, which is Job speaking as one who looks only to the grave.
